[242/1873]: Can network meta-analysis rankings be calibrated against registry enrollment denominators to detect when pooled comparisons rely on disproportionately small evidence fractions? We developed a denominator-calibrated NMA framework augmenting contrast-based network meta-analysis with registry-derived ClinicalTrials.gov enrollment to weight comparisons by evidence mass. The calibration applies an enrollment-adjusted information fraction to each network edge, penalising comparisons where the pooled sample is under 20 percent of registered enrollment for that pair. Treatment rankings shifted for 3 of 12 comparisons in the test network when denominator calibration was applied, with the largest shift occurring where the published evidence covered only 8 percent of registered enrollment. Living updates monitor new registry entries and flag when published evidence fractions change by more than 5 percentage points. Denominator calibration could alert users when NMA rankings are driven by selectively published subsets of registered evidence. The framework depends on accurate ClinicalTrials.gov enrollment reporting and cannot detect unpublished trials that were never registered.
